item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-b273e2acb8c0ee0e","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 1 June 2023, Justice Minister Rose Mutombo and ICC Prosecutor Karim Khan signed an agreement to strengthen cooperation on genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes; the agreement was intended to facilitate ICC activities in the DRC. The presidency reported that Tshisekedi reaffirmed attachment to the Rome Statute and determination to pursue the rule of law.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.9","3B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; presidential website account of a formal cooperation agreement and stated commitment.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi was present, publicly endorsed the cooperation, and was described as determined to pursue the rule of law.","limitations":["The source does not document subsequent implementation, prosecutions, convictions, or remedies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b273e2acb8c0ee0e","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Before the June 2023 ICC cooperation ceremony, the Congolese government invited the ICC to initiate an investigation into alleged crimes by the RDF/M23 coalition in eastern DRC.","question_ids":["2B.9","3B.4","3B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly linked to the 2023 ICC mission and government request.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the invitation to the government under Tshisekedi's presidency, but does not identify the individual decision-maker.","limitations":["The allegation and request are reported without an outcome or independent verification in the document."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6e6261afc86b9ca8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 7 March 2023, Tshisekedi inaugurated a new CENAREF building while the government presented a new law addressing money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing involving weapons of mass destruction.","question_ids":["1B.6","1B.9","5B.5","7B.10","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; formal institutional and legislative actions are reported.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi inaugurated the facility; the source presents the law and strengthened institutional framework as part of his governance priorities.","limitations":["The source does not provide the law's text, budget, enforcement record, or independent assessment of CENAREF effectiveness."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6e6261afc86b9ca8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The presidency described CENAREF, alongside the Inspectorate General of Finance, APLC, and Court of Accounts, as part of an institutional apparatus intended to strengthen good governance and combat corruption.","question_ids":["5B.5","7B.6","7B.10","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly reported in a March 2023 presidential account.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies these institutions as measures associated with Tshisekedi's anti-corruption priorities.","limitations":["This is an official characterization and does not establish independent institutional autonomy or enforcement outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-656c74f787c7e413","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 15 September 2023, 69 newly appointed senior magistrates of the Court of Cassation, Council of State, and associated general prosecutors took constitutional oaths before Tshisekedi and formally entered office.","question_ids":["4B.4","8B.2","8B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; formal judicial appointments and assumption of office are documented.","ruler_attribution":"The magistrates had been appointed by presidential orders publicized on 15 August 2023; Tshisekedi received their oaths as supreme magistrate.","limitations":["The source does not establish selection quality, independence, tenure protection, later performance, or political influence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-656c74f787c7e413","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The August 2023 presidential judicial reorganization included promotions, dismissals, retirements, and compulsory resignations, and was presented as part of reforms intended to consolidate the rule of law.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.5","7B.5","8B.4","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the source reports formal personnel changes and their stated rationale.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the appointments and other personnel actions to Tshisekedi through presidential ordinances.","limitations":["The document gives no reasons for individual removals and no independent assessment of whether the changes strengthened judicial independence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-13d5db718abe1375","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 8 June 2023, four senior Constitutional Court prosecutors took oaths before Tshisekedi; one prosecutor received a second presidentially appointed term, three first attorneys-general were appointed on 6 June, and Masiala Kaza became the first woman to hold that senior judicial rank in the country.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.7","4B.8","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the ceremony and appointments are dated.","ruler_attribution":"The source states that Tshisekedi appointed the officials by presidential order and presided over the oath ceremony.","limitations":["The source does not assess independence, competence, political neutrality, or the court's subsequent decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80a4d75c08e8e6a6","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"FAO reports that the DRC has a complex humanitarian crisis driven by armed conflict, natural disasters, and disease outbreaks, compounded by currency depreciation, high food prices, extreme poverty, and structural weaknesses; agricultural assistance is identified as a means to support vulnerable households.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","5B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The supplied page is a 2026 country emergency profile, not a period-specific 2023 assessment; it provides context but limited direct 2023 fit.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to Tshisekedi or his government is made.","limitations":["The page reports 2026 figures and does not isolate 2023 conditions, presidential decisions, or causal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ade7f78ecc160ac2","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In August 2023, the strategic steering committee reviewing Tshisekedi's Local Development Programme for 145 Territories reported that more than 300 to 400 works were ready, despite difficulties in some eastern territories; the programme's planned outputs included approximately 1,200 schools, 500–700 health centres, and 145 administrative buildings.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the report covers implementation progress as of August.","ruler_attribution":"The programme is identified as a flagship programme of President Tshisekedi; implementation was supervised by a government committee chaired by the prime minister.","limitations":["The figures are government-reported; the source does not provide independent verification, completed-service quality, distributional incidence, or total budget execution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dcc4358e2be24dd5","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 18 October 2023, as supreme commander, Tshisekedi directed the FARDC to form a single corps defending state institutions and the population, urged loyalty to the nation rather than personal interests, and promised government support for soldiers and their families.","question_ids":["2B.8","3B.2","3B.9","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; a dated presidential military directive and commitment are reported.","ruler_attribution":"The directive and commitments were issued personally by Tshisekedi as commander-in-chief.","limitations":["The source does not document implementation, military spending, rules of engagement, disciplinary action, or effects on violence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dcc4358e2be24dd5","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"During the October 2023 military address, Tshisekedi acknowledged that insecurity in eastern DRC placed the country in a delicate phase and expressed confidence that the government and armed forces would win the conflict.","question_ids":["2B.3","3B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly within 2023; the statement concerns the ongoing eastern conflict.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment and reassurance were made by Tshisekedi as commander-in-chief.","limitations":["The source provides rhetoric rather than evidence of defensive necessity, alternatives, operational decisions, or outcome."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c14ae8bd8790fba","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"CFR reported that the December 2023 elections were chaotic and extended beyond the scheduled election day, with widespread irregularities; opposition and observer groups challenged the process, and Tshisekedi was preliminarily declared the winner.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.10","7B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in January 2024 but concerns the December 2023 election within the target period.","ruler_attribution":"Tshisekedi was the incumbent and preliminary winner; the source does not establish that he personally caused each irregularity.","limitations":["The report predates final judicial confirmation and relies partly on observer and civil-society accounts summarized by CFR."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c14ae8bd8790fba","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"CFR summarized reports of illegible voter cards, missing equipment, intimidation, more than 5,000 incidents reported to Catholic and Protestant church observers, mishandling of sensitive materials by electoral agents, and a non-transparent tabulation process.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reported incidents occurred during the December 2023 elections.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes operational failures to electoral agents and authorities; it does not directly prove Tshisekedi ordered or personally conducted them.","limitations":["The document does not identify which incidents were independently verified or describe corrective action by the president."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c14ae8bd8790fba","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"CFR stated that authorities had indicated attempts to address political grievances through protest would be quashed forcefully, and characterized the judiciary as compromised and unlikely to provide effective redress for election-irregularity complaints.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.10","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The assessment concerns the post-election environment in late 2023, though the article was published in January 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source refers broadly to authorities and does not attribute the statements or judicial condition directly to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["This is an external analytical assessment; the supplied text does not identify specific orders, cases, or protest incidents."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-37b3af166d8b363a","SRC-9c77ff0dd2b10bf9","SRC-7eddca686f4d4f91","SRC-2efc598a12809e59"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied pages are undated, current-period, generic, 404 pages, or index pages and therefore do not provide concrete, period-fitting facts about Tshisekedi during 2023.","The supplied evidence is predominantly official government reporting or high-level external analysis; it provides limited independent verification of implementation, outcomes, budget execution, judicial independence, or personal responsibility."]}
